0.original: Beq Lugg is ready to speak of the metaphysical.

26.original: Search Mount Biran Mines for lumps of pristine clay.

27.original: Deliver the lumps of pristine clay to Beq Lugg.

48.original: Corporeal and incorporeal aether... I confess I have never had cause to make the distinction.

49.original: Did they just say what I think they said? Might there really be a way to help Halric and the others? And help ourselves in the process?

51.original: I suspect the Crystal Exarch has told you of my past. That I was once a mage of the royal court of Voeburt, and that soulcraft was my field of study.

52.original: The tonic you administered to the patients here is one of the fruits of my labors. I hoped to do great things for the kingdom...

53.original: <sigh> But in the end, my knowledge brought only suffering. A plague the like of which none had ever seen.

54.original: In the hands of unscrupulous men, what should have been my greatest triumph instead became my greatest shame...

56.original: You mustn't dwell in the past.

57.original: And now you have a chance to redeem yourself.

58.original: At least the Warriors of Light brought those responsible to justice.

59.original: I know that only too well. Alas, the knowledge we require is steeped in such bitter memories.

60.original: That I do. A comforting thought indeed.

61.original: Aye, that they did. I shudder to think what might have happened had they not.

62.original: But let us return to the task at hand─finding a means by which we might revitalize these people's incorporeal aether.

63.original: Do you think it can be done?

64.original: Were the skies still ablaze with primordial Light, I would call it an exercise in futility. But now─now we may have a chance.

65.original: The method I have in mind will entail the conjuring of a familiar. They are able to amplify the energies poured into them, making them the perfect conduit for the aether-revitalizing magicks we will ultimately employ.

66.original: If you're about to launch into a lengthy explanation of the metaphysics of your plan─don't bother. I'd rather get on with doing whatever it is that needs to be done, if it's all the same to you.

67.original: Whatever reagents must be procured, or spells invoked─I'll do it.

69.original: Very well. Your first task will be to gather the necessary materials.

70.original: The purest of waters and finest of clays, as well as a fae lantern brimming with pixie magick.

71.original: If you're <hex:021A020203>convinced<hex:021A020103> the resulting familiar could help the patients─fine.

72.original: Alphinaud─the water and clay will be simple enough, but I think you know what we'll have to do to get the lantern.

74.original: The pixies took quite a liking to us before. If we humor them with our company, I'm sure they'll be willing to help us.

76.original: ...<hex:021A020203>Fine<hex:021A020103>. We'll pay a visit to Il Mheg. Though I never thought <hex:021A020203>you<hex:021A020103> would be the one to suggest going back there.

77.original: I'm impressed you've been there at all, let alone befriended the fae folk.

78.original: Oh, while you're about it, seek out the Nu Mou of Pla Enni. They will be able to supply you with water suitable for our needs.

79.original: Right. Let's get this over with, shall we.

80.original: There still remains the matter of the clay. Might I prevail upon you to find it?

81.original: Clay from Amh Araeng would likely be best. Know you of anyone who might be able to assist us?

83.original: I could ask the miners at Twine.

84.original: Well, there are the scavengers at Mord Souq.

85.original: Ah, yes! They will be able to point you in the right direction, I am sure.

86.original: Scavengers, you say? Well...they may know the lie of the land, but I daresay they are more interested in the trinkets and baubles hiding in the earth than the earth itself. Now, miners on the other hand...

87.original: What's that? You know the miners of Twine? Perfect! Speak with them and you should have no trouble procuring what we need.

88.original: While you and the twins are occupied, I will see if there is aught else I can learn of the stagnation which afflicts the people here.

89.original: I have no doubt that the miners of Twine can help you find what we need. While you are away, I will do what I can to learn more about the nature of the patients' affliction.

90.original: I can't stop thinking about that giant Talos we built. Can you imagine what it could do with a matching trolley? It feels like a waste <hex:021A020203>not<hex:021A020103> to build one.

91.original: <sigh> Sometimes I wish we'd never got that trolley running again. Now Jeryk wants <hex:021A020203>more<hex:021A020103> of the bloody things, and refuses to shut up about it.

93.original: You've come at a good time. We've just this moment finished repairing the Talos and trolley you lot took to Nabaath Areng.

94.original: The trolley was no trouble, but the Talos would have been another matter, had we not had a visit from Master Chai.

95.original: He offered us a share of the leftover building materials from Daedalus Stoneworks, as well as a few trade secrets to help us along.

96.original: Clever man, that Chai-Nuzz. He seemed pretty keen on the ideas I had for putting the giant Talos to work.

97.original: Like a giant trolley! But Magnus still refuses to see all the good we could do with it...

98.original: You're entitled to your dreams, Jeryk, but that doesn't mean you can go harassing our guests with them. Master Chai was just being polite.

99.original: And something tells me <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203> here didn't come all this way to talk about trolleys. What is it you need, friend?

100.original: I see. And this...familiar requires clay from Amh Araeng.

101.original: Well, look no further. If anyone can find you some quality clay, it's us.

102.original: Saying that, it isn't exactly a commodity nowadays... But there must be some lurking somewhere or other, waiting to be dug up.

103.original: If I'm not mistaken, there was a time when they used to take clay from Mount Biran Mines to make adobe bricks.

104.original: Place is swarming with coyotes now, but if you're after the good stuff, you could do worse than to look there.

105.original: I still say a trolley for that Talos is a good idea. You agree, don't you?

106.original: You'll want to be on your guard at the mines. Spend too long peering at the ground, and a coyote is sure to come and bite you on the arse.

107.original: Stay safe out there. And remember: you don't need an excuse to come and visit us.

108.original: The pixies were constantly confusing me with Alisaie. In jest, I assume. I mean, it's not as if we look <hex:021A020203>that<hex:021A020103> much alike!<hex:02100103>We, uh...don't look that much alike, do we?

109.original: That had better be the only thing we need from the pixies. If I have to endure one more prank, so help me gods...

110.original: The twins have returned, and in one piece at that. I was convinced the pixies would turn at least one of them into a garden ornament...but no.

111.original: ...You have the clay, I take it?

112.original: Wonderful. We need but combine the clay and the water, then heat the mixture with the fae lantern. After that, it will be a simple matter of settling upon a suitable form, and performing the necessary incantation.

113.original: Beq Lugg. I have a question. In the event that we had need of this spell and you weren't around, would it be possible for another to perform the incantation?

114.original: Assuming they possessed the requisite skill, yes.

115.original: Halric and the others have suffered so much, and I swore to do everything in my power to save them. If there is a chance this spell could do that, I would be the one to invoke it.

116.original: ...Hmmm. Mayhap you <hex:021A020203>should<hex:021A020103> be the one to do so.

117.original: A deep understanding of the subjects' physical state, combined with a strong desire to help them, can drastically increase the magick's effect. And you are plainly more familiar with these people than I.

118.original: I daresay there are few in all of Norvrandt more dedicated to finding a cure. Is that not so, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>?

120.original: Absolutely. She's the best woman for the job.

121.original: Very few. But if aught should go awry...I'll see what I can do.

122.original: I'll give it my all. For Halric. For Tesleen...

123.original: Is that a challenge? Well, I'll be damned if I let it come to that.

124.original: Then we are all of a mind on the matter. Alisaie shall be the one to conjure the familiar.

125.original: By the Twelve! Though it was only for a moment, he spoke! There may yet be hope for these people!

126.original: The girl's resolve is quite impressive. One might almost think she drew strength from another...

128.original: How is he, Beq Lugg? Did it work?

129.original: I believe it did. You and your fledgling familiar have done well.

130.original: If my eyes do not deceive, a hint of color has returned to his soul.

131.original: Gods... I would jump for joy if I weren't so exhausted.

133.original: As you are even now in the process of discovering, this magick asks much of the invoker. What you may <hex:021A020203>not<hex:021A020103> have realized is that the same is also true of the subject. As such, we must proceed with caution. However, with further treatment, I have the utmost confidence the boy will make a full recovery.

134.original: Observing the reanimation of his stagnant soul has been most enlightening. I will need time to put my theories to the proof, but I believe I can fashion a spell to produce the opposite effect. That is, to <hex:021A020203>induce<hex:021A020103> stagnation.

135.original: Thus enabling our safe transport back to the Source via auracite!

136.original: A thought occurred to me─about this treatment.

137.original: Beq Lugg said when the soul is rendered dormant, the mind is separated from the body. That a person becomes incapable of interacting with the world around them.

138.original: Does that not sound a lot like some of the tempered back in the Source?

139.original: Not really. It is the fate of most tempered to become slaves to primals─save in a handful of cases. Or am I missing something?

140.original: If I can master this technique─the art of revitalizing the soul─I know of at least one in the Source who could desperately use such treatment.

144.original: Do you really think it could work?

145.original: <hex:021A020203>Ga Bu<hex:021A020103>. His condition is eerily similar to Halric and the others', the only difference being that his soul was suffused with earth-aspected aether from summoning Titan, rather than Light. It follows that if his soul is subject to a similar kind of stagnation, there may be a chance we can save him...right?

146.original: Exactly! His condition is uncannily similar to Halric's, is it not? The only difference being that his soul was suffused with earth-aspected aether instead of Light. It follows that if his soul is subject to a similar kind of stagnation, there may be a chance we can save him...right?

147.original: Why shouldn't it? Ga Bu's condition is virtually identical to Halric's, is it not? The only difference being that his soul was suffused with earth-aspected aether instead of Light. It follows that if his soul is subject to a similar kind of stagnation, there may be a chance we can save him.

148.original: Forgive me, but who is this Ga Bu fellow of whom you speak?

149.original: ...I see. His condition does sound similar...yet there is much and more about the soul that remains unknown even to me. I say this not to discourage you, you understand, but to remind you that this is delicate work we do here. Work requiring <hex:021A020203>patience<hex:021A020103>.

150.original: Of course. And as long as there is hope for the patients here, I will devote whatever time is needed to see this through.

151.original: But I refuse to spend that time in idleness. If it's all the same to you, I'd like to stay here with Angelo and continue with their treatment.

152.original: The two of you should return to the Crystarium with Beq Lugg and see if you can't make some headway with their newly posited theories.

153.original: I would tell you to rest first, but I see you're not to be convinced. Ah, the fire of youth.

154.original: Let us return to the Crystarium, then.

156.original: Kai-Shirr!? What are you doing all the way out here?

157.original: There's trouble back in Eulmore. Lady Chai's beside herself. Sighing, pacing, the whole lot. Near enough <hex:021A020203>begged<hex:021A020103> me to go and find you.

158.original: ...Sighing <hex:021A020203>and<hex:021A020103> pacing, you say? It must be urgent.

159.original: I take it I will be returning to the Crystarium alone. Go on, then. It's not as if I have anything for you to do.

161.original: Sorry for bothering you and all that, but she says the future of Eulmore's at stake.
